content.text:
**Finding submitted: compliant (sits at the fallback).**

Summary of the review:

| Element (fallback) | Where satisfied |
|---|---|
| Commitment limited to current 12-month term | §13 (p0078) — 1-year term, one-year renewals, 30-day non-renewal notice |
| Reducible on ~30 days' notice | §14 (p0079) — Client may terminate at will; fees run only to month-end following notice, with no unused-balance payment |
| Shortfall via true-up, not penalty | §5(a) (p0045) — pay-up-to-floor mechanic; no shortfall fee, liquidated damages or acceleration anywhere |

No redline was proposed. The minimum monthly fee in §5(a) falls short of our preferred "usage only" position, but because we keep an unqualified convenience exit that does not require paying the balance of the year's minimums, the bargain meets the fallback on its material terms and the playbook directs that we accept it rather than upgrade to preferred wording.

Two items flagged in the rationale as commentary only, not deviations:
- §6 (p0047) strips our right to supporting documentation for, and to contest, the minimum monthly fees — a billing-dispute point rather than a commitment point, and better raised under the invoicing/audit rule if one applies.
- The dollar amounts in §5(a) (and the Exhibit A/B schedules) are still blank and must be settled before signature; the fallback analysis assumes a floor no greater than our expected run-rate usage.
